name: Portugal
tagline: Cheap for EU students, but the EU route is the Portuguese one
summary: An EU citizen cannot use Portugal's international-student route. Public universities are reached through the Concurso Nacional de Acesso, the same national contest Portuguese school-leavers use, at a capped fee of €697 a year (2025/26). It runs late, in July and August, after IB results, but it mostly leads to Portuguese-taught degrees. The private Universidade Católica takes applications directly, in English, on predicted grades.
whyConsider: Public tuition is capped: €697 a year for a licenciatura in 2025/26, and an EU student pays exactly that.
The national contest runs after IB results, so you apply with real grades.
Católica Lisbon runs English-taught business and economics bachelors open to any nationality, applied to directly.
watchOuts: As an EU citizen you are not an 'international student' in Portugal, so the English-language international routes at Porto, Nova SBE and elsewhere are closed to you.
In 2026, IB candidates substituting their IB exams for Portuguese entrance exams had to apply by 29 July, a week earlier than everyone else.
You need an equivalence certificate for the IB Diploma, with apostilled and translated documents, before you can apply.
Most public-university degrees are taught in Portuguese.

ibRecognition.gradeConversion: Your IB result becomes a secondary grade on the Portuguese 0–200 scale through an equivalence certificate. Entrance exams (provas de ingresso) can be replaced by IB exams only if they are on the list the CNAES publishes by 31 May each year.

language.englishTaughtBachelors: Small: mainly business and economics, at Católica Lisbon and Nova SBE.
notes: The national contest leads mostly to Portuguese-taught degrees.

feeContext.summary: Public institutions charge at most €697 a year for a licenciatura or integrated master's. Private institutions set their own: Católica Lisbon charges EU students €780 a month over ten months in 2026-27.
Under the international-student statute each institution sets its own fee: €3,500–€16,500 a year at the University of Porto for 2026/27. Católica Lisbon charges €858 a month over ten months.

sectorLandscape.summary: A binary system: ensino universitário at universities and ensino politécnico at polytechnic institutes, each public or private. Public places are filled through the national contest; private institutions admit directly. Polytechnics also run the CTeSP, a two-year professional course outside the contest.

routes.what: Lisbon, Porto, Coimbra, Minho, Aveiro, NOVA and others. Three-year licenciatura; public places allocated by the national contest.
More applied licenciaturas in engineering, business, health and the arts, also through the national contest for public places.
routes.note: None is listed on this page; not covered here.

routes.what: Universidade Católica Portuguesa and others, admitting directly on their own terms and fees. Where most English-taught bachelors open to an EU applicant are.
Two years, 120 ECTS, with a work placement, mostly at polytechnics. Not a degree; applied to directly at the institution.

jurisdictions.name: Public universities — through the national contest
jurisdictions.summary: An EU applicant reaches every public institution through the Concurso Nacional de Acesso run by DGES, in July and August, at the capped fee.

variations.label: Deadlines
variations.summary: 2026 precedent: candidates substituting foreign exams applied 20–29 July, others to 6 August; results 23 August. The 2027 calendar is not yet published.

jurisdictions.name: Universidade Católica — direct
jurisdictions.summary: A private university outside the national contest. Applies directly, in English for its international bachelors, on predicted grades, to any nationality.

notes: Nova SBE is public: an EU applicant reaches it through the national contest, not its international route.

Not established: the 2027 national contest calendar, the 2026/27 and 2027/28 propina cap on an official page (press reports say it stayed at €697 for 2026/27), Católica's 2027 dates, and whether a CTeSP accepts an IB Diploma.
